Somos estudiantes de Ingeniería en tecnología de software, y somos amantes de este nuevo mundo tecnológico. Tenemos, ya experiencia en otros eventos tecnológicos y hackhatones. 

Hoy buscamos implementar nuestros conocimientos en resolver los desafíos y problemas que la NASA nos ofrece, para lograr resaltar y lograr lo inimaginable.
summary: KANAN by S.A.R.A. (Radar and Anomaly Analysis System) is an open-source environmental diagnostic web platform that converts NASA-ISRO NISAR radar data and NASA FIRMS thermal anomalies into verifiable decisions for the Yucatán Peninsula. Built for the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge, KANAN goes beyond passive map viewers by fusing multi-sensor telemetry pixel by pixel. It reads calibrated NISAR L2 GCOV backscatter products (HVHV polarization) via ASF DAAC to measure surface echo loss and gain in hectares between two dates, crossing them with VIIRS thermal detections from NASA FIRMS and optical indices (NDVI/MNDWI) from NASA HLS. This fusion classifies surface changes to separate wildfires and agricultural burns from floods, vegetation loss, or hurricane impacts. To make complex SAR imagery accessible, KANAN features an interactive Action Center, an Echo Loupe for visual radar validation, educational simulators, a pedagogical Copilot, and a hallucination-free hybrid AI engine where deterministic rules set the probable cause and a numeric verifier audits every figure before exporting a 5-block field report.
details:
KANAN by S.A.R.A. is an open-source environmental diagnostic web platform designed to solve a critical problem: when hurricanes, floods, or wildfires hit the Yucatán Peninsula, clouds blind optical satellites. NASA-ISRO NISAR radar can see through clouds, but SAR data is difficult to interpret for non-experts. KANAN democratizes this data by transforming raw telemetry into verifiable field decisions.

How it works: The platform allows users to select a region and two dates. The backend ingests real NASA-ISRO NISAR L2 GCOV (L-band, HVHV) products from ASF DAAC using partial HTTP Range reads. It applies statistical change detection (boxcar filter, logarithmic ratio, and 3σ threshold) to measure backscatter decrease (red) or increase (blue) in hectares. It then fuses this radar change pixel by pixel with VIIRS thermal anomalies from NASA FIRMS and NDVI/MNDWI optical indices from NASA HLS to classify the terrain into 6 categories, separating wildfires from floods or vegetation loss.

AI & UX Innovation: We built a hybrid AI engine (Gemini 3.6 Flash) guarded by a deterministic mathematical rule engine. The backend determines the probable cause based on the multi-sensor spatial intersection, and a strict numeric verifier ensures the AI never hallucinates a single hectare before generating a downloadable 5-block scientific report. The frontend features an interactive Action Center, an Echo Loupe for visual radar validation, a pedagogical Copilot chatbot with 16-turn memory, and a 3D interactive globe with NISAR's orbit built in SVG layers to ensure zero lag.

Impact: KANAN empowers park rangers (CONANP), civil protection teams, and researchers to protect critical mangroves and wetlands. By reducing the payload by 95% and utilizing spatial index structures (STRtree), our system delivers lightning-fast responses (0.42 ms for cached queries), proving that complex NASA data can be accessible, actionable, and scientifically honest on a standard laptop.

Tech Stack: Frontend: PWA, JavaScript ES Modules, MapLibre GL JS. Backend: Python 3.13, FastAPI, NumPy, rasterio, shapely 2.0 (STRtree), orjson, SQLite.
